_meta.indication: SABRIL is indicated as adjunctive therapy for adult patients with refractory complex partial seizures (CPS) who have inadequately responded to several alternative treatments and for whom the potential benefits outweigh the risk of vision loss; not indicated as a first line agent for complex partial seizures
_meta.receipt_date: Received May 2, 1994 (original NDA); complete response submitted December 28, 2007

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-arm trial; 8-week baseline followed by 16 to 18 week experimental phase; two arms (placebo and 3 grams/day)
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with a documented history of CPS or partial seizures with secondary generalization, on 1-2 AEDs, with a history of failure of carbamazepine or phenytoin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction in mean monthly seizure frequency of all partial seizures from baseline
pivotal_trials.result: Median monthly CPS frequency fell from 8.5 to 5.5 with 3 g/day SABRIL (N=84) vs 9.0 to 7.0 with placebo (N=89); P<0.05 compared to placebo

pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-arm trial with 4 arms (placebo, 1 gram/day, 3 grams/day and 6 grams/day); 8-week baseline followed by 16 to 18 week experimental phase
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with refractory complex partial seizures, on 1-2 AEDs with a history of failure of carbamazepine or phenytoin
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Reduction in mean monthly seizure frequency of all partial seizures from baseline
pivotal_trials.result: Median monthly CPS frequency fell from 7.0 to 3.5 with 3 g/day (N=41) and from 8.5 to 3.5 with 6 g/day (N=41); placebo (N=44) 8.8 to 8.2; P<0.05 compared to placebo for 3 and 6 g/day; 1 g/day (N=45) was not effective

key_safety: Most serious risk is permanent progressive bilateral concentric visual field constriction in 30 percent or more of patients. Most common adverse reactions (≥5% over placebo) include fatigue (28% SABRIL vs 15% placebo), somnolence (24% vs 10%), nystagmus, tremor (15 (3 g) vs 8 placebo), vision blurred, memory impairment, weight gain and confusional state
target_moa: Vigabatrin is an irreversible inhibitor of gamma-aminobutyric acid transaminase (GABA-T), the enzyme responsible for metabolism of GABA, resulting in increased CNS levels of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: VISION LOSS — SABRIL causes progressive and permanent bilateral concentric visual field constriction in a high percentage of patients; risk increases with total dose and duration, but no exposure is known that is free of risk of vision loss

rems.type: A REMS was required, consisting of a Medication Guide, communication plan, and elements to assure safe use; SABRIL is available only through a special restricted distribution program (SHARE)

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee was convened on 1/7/09 and 1/8/09; for CPS no formal vote was taken but the committee agreed SABRIL should be reserved for patients refractory to several anticonvulsants and available only under restricted conditions

description.text: Added paradoxical bronchospasms to the Postmarketing Experience section of the label

citations.quote: This Changes Being Effected supplemental new drug application provides for the inclusion of paradoxical bronchospasms in the Postmarketing Experience section of the Breo Ellipta label.

description.text: Expanded use to patients 2 years of age and older with refractory complex partial seizures

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sNDAs provide for expanding the use of Sabril to patients 2 years of age and older with refractory complex partial seizures (rCPS) and proposed modifications to the approved vigabatrin REMS. These Prior Approval sNDAs also provide for revisions to the Sabril labeling to comply with the Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule (PLLR).

summary.text: SABRIL (vigabatrin) tablets received a traditional NDA approval for adjunctive therapy in adult refractory complex partial seizures after a prolonged regulatory history including Not Approvable letters (1995, 1998) and an Approvable letter (1997); approval was conditioned on a required REMS (including the SHARE restricted distribution program) and post-marketing requirements covering pediatric study and vision-loss safety

citations.quote: This new drug application provides for the use of Sabril (vigabatrin) Tablets for Refractory Complex Partial Seizures in Adults.
Reference is also made to the Agency's Not Approvable Letter dated April 28, 1995, Approvable Letter dated November 26, 1997, and Not Approvable Letter dated October 27, 1998.

In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for Sabril (vigabatrin) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of vision loss and of suicidal thoughts and behaviors.
